ownership_reason: Only the gold visits the elements of the array; hop 1 checks the array reference, hops 2-4 pass the array and the object along unchanged. The gold never matches a null element, so no one-line pre-filter of the object can make a null slot match, no one-line utility of this code base replaces the null elements of an Object[], removing a null element shifts every later index, and a -1 result cannot be turned back into a position without searching again. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the facade's javadoc ('the object to find, may be null'); the 3-arg overloads ArrayUtils.lastIndexOf(Object[], Object, int) and ArrayUtils.indexOf(Object[], Object, int) match a null object against null elements (testLastIndexOfWithStartIndex: lastIndexOf(array, null, 5) == 4; testIndexOf: indexOf(array, null) == 4; testContains: contains(array, null)); ObjectUtils.equals(null, null) is true (ObjectUtilsTest.testEquals). The gold's javadoc promises the last occurrence of the given object in the array, which for the trigger's null object is index 4.
